web_bottleneck: Vertiv relieves the AI data-center power and thermal bottleneck - grid-interconnect delays and rising heat density. It buys upstream for speed: UIG microgrid and behind-the-meter power to accelerate time to power (2026-09-02); KES and ThermoKey add fluid and heat-rejection capacity (2026-09-24, 2026-06-12). Its own constraint is capacity ramp and supply-chain congestion (2026-07-29).
web_who_benefits_next: Second and third order: liquid-cooling fluid and component suppliers, switchgear, transformer and energy-storage makers, onsite-generation and utility firms, plus the semiconductor partners the CEO cites (2026-02-11). Sellers of UIG and KES can earn up to $1.15B earnout (2026-09-02). No dated primary source confirms specific third-party beneficiaries.
web_who_loses: Rival integrated critical-infrastructure vendors competing on combined power and cooling, and standalone microgrid or fluid-management specialists, lose share and European beachheads as Vertiv buys ThermoKey (2026-06-12), UIG (2026-09-02) and KES (2026-09-24). Utility-interconnect-dependent developers lose leverage as behind-the-meter power improves (2026-09-02).

web_did_they_deliver: So far yes. After promising momentum (2026-02-11), Q1 2026 sales rose 30pc and FY26 guidance was raised (2026-04-22); Q2 2026 rose 24pc and guidance was raised again to $13.8-14.2B and adjusted EPS $6.65-6.75 (2026-07-29). FY26 guide moved from $13.25-13.75B and $5.97-6.07 (Feb) to $13.8-14.2B and $6.65-6.75 (Jul).
web_what_would_falsify: A Q3 2026 result (expected October; IR date unconfirmed) below the 34-36pc organic guide, or a cut to FY26 $13.8-14.2B and adjusted EPS $6.65-6.75; backlog failing to convert (book-to-bill below ~1.0x); EMEA organic staying negative past 2026; either Q4-2026 acquisition closing failing; or tariffs flipping price-cost negative.
